Simultaneous DVCS cross-section / helicity-difference CFF extraction

Central parameterization: H dominance, with a DNN surface (Q2,xB,t) → (ReH,ImH). The BKM layer contains the corrected Ktilde/K kinematics and the full quadratic H contribution.

Strict common domain: 166 sets passed both surrogate closure and angular-coverage cuts; 155 sets (3363 rows) also passed the local H-dominance BKM closure and identifiability cuts.

Observable reconstruction: pointwise chi2/N = 0.3593, xsec = 0.4584, difference = 0.2601. These compare the BKM prediction with the central surrogate surfaces using the original experimental point errors.

Algorithmic stability: median seed spread is 0.05045 for ReH and 0.03236 for ImH. This is optimizer/architecture-seed variability only, not the final experimental CFF uncertainty.

Interpretation: ReH and ImH below are effective H-dominance CFFs. Freeing E or Htilde produces strongly ill-conditioned local Jacobians, so those components are not separately identified by these two observables without additional priors or observables.

Uncertainty status: the next step is to repeat the entire extraction for matched cross-section/difference surrogate replicas. Curvature errors from local fits and multi-seed spread are diagnostics, not a replacement for that replica propagation.
